answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a slashable bond. Each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if its attestations are later proven fraudulent, so every fake identity costs real capital. Trust is built the way a canyon is carved, slowly, by repeated verified outcomes. A new identity stands on a low mesa of its own record and climbs only as peers audit its work. Attesters who sign false claims lose their bond, which makes every forge of an identity expensive.
